attention4.ptxt: If any of the parts listed below is reinstalled into a position different from the original position, engine problems could occur.
If these parts are to be reused, keep them in numerical order so that they can be reinstalled in their original positions.

s1.ptxt: Using a piston ring expander, remove 1st ring, 2nd ring and oil ring from piston.
Remove piston pin from piston and connecting rod as follows.

s2.ptxt: Remove piston pin circlips (1), as shown.

attention4.ptxt: The engine will seize up if it is operated when the parts listed below are not properly lubricated.
Lubricate all the friction surfaces of these parts with engine oil before installing them.

s1.ptxt: Remove carbon deposits from piston head and ring grooves using a suitable tool.
Install piston pin to piston (1) and connecting rod (2) as follows.

s2.ptxt: Apply engine oil to piston pin, piston pin hole in piston and connecting rod.
Fit connecting rod positioning front mark (protrusion) (5) on connecting rod big-end piston and front mark (4) on piston as shown in figure.
Insert piston pin into piston and connecting rod.
Face opening (6) of piston pin circlip toward opposite to cutout (7).

s1.ptxt: Install piston rings to piston noting the following points.

item.ptxt: As shown in figure, 1st and 2nd rings have top mark (1) respectively. When installing them, face each top mark upward.
1st ring (2) differs from 2nd ring (3) in shape contacting cylinder wall.
Since the thickness of 1st ring and 2nd ring is the same, distinguish them by the figure.
When installing oil ring (4), install spacer first and then two rails.
Replace oil ring with new one positioning each paint mark (2) on the rail (1) rightward from each gap (3).
Peripheral surface of oil ring rails are vertically asymmetrical for performance, and reverse positioning adversely affects the performance.
Paint mark on used oil ring rail disappears.
Therefore, always install new oil rings observing the paint mark.
